challenges.name: match-enums-readonly-quiz
challenges.title: Predict it: switch, match, enums and readonly
challenges.description: Compare switch and match on the same value, then pick the rules for backed enums, readonly properties and match without a default.

questions.explanation: switch compares with ==, and '0' == false is true (the string '0' is falsy), so the first case matches and prints A. That case has no break, so execution falls through into the next case and prints B, then stops at break: AB. match compares with === and has no fall-through: '0' === false is false, '0' === '0' is true, so it returns B. The whole output is "AB B".

questions.question: enum OrderStatus: string { case Paid = 'paid'; case Shipped = 'shipped'; } and final readonly class Shipment { public function __construct(public string $orderId, public OrderStatus $status) {} }. Which statements are true? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: from() accepts only an exact backing value and throws a ValueError otherwise ("Shipped" is not a valid backing value for enum OrderStatus); tryFrom() returns null instead, which is the version for input you expect to be invalid sometimes. Every enum case is a single object, so OrderStatus::Paid === OrderStatus::from('paid') is true and enum values compare safely with ===. A readonly property can be initialised once, from inside the class, and never changed again - not even by a method of the same class: "Cannot modify readonly property Shipment::$status"; to change a status, create a new object. And match without a matching arm and without default throws an UnhandledMatchError instead of returning null.

options.text: A method of Shipment may assign $this->status = OrderStatus::Shipped

challenges.name: order-status-enum
challenges.title: Model order statuses with a backed enum and match
challenges.description: The warehouse app of Hồ Gươm Books reports order statuses as strings, and a switch with a missing break and a catch-all default sent customers the wrong emails. Complete the backed enum OrderStatus: its six cases, a Vietnamese label for each, and canMoveTo, which allows only the moves of the order life cycle. The test runner turns every event into an enum with tryFrom, applies the moves your enum allows and prints what happened to each order.

tests.name: A normal order from payment to delivery
tests.input:
HG-24117 paid
HG-24117 shipped
HG-24117 delivered
tests.expected:
HG-24117: pending -> paid
HG-24117: paid -> shipped
HG-24117: shipped -> delivered
HG-24117 delivered (Đã giao)

tests.name: Moves that skip a step or go back are rejected

HG-24121 returned (Đã trả hàng)
